purpose: Phase 1 of the timing campaign: prove the timing-analysis instruments exist and are functional (with a sensitivity control), rather than classifying them absent.
revision_note: Revision 2 makes the toolchain survive court recreation and unblocks perf. The revision-1 record described a hand-installed toolchain living in a running container's writable layer, with perf BLOCKED by a missing capability. Both are fixed by docker/openssl-rs-court-tools.Dockerfile (the toolchain as an image layer) and --cap-add=CAP_PERFMON at container creation. Revision-1 negatives are preserved (see tools[].historical_status, venue_history and install_replay_ephemeral); nothing was deleted to make the new result look better.

source.head: 32a4b78280cd565949d8c4205942c35b18520401
source.head_subject: timing tools: install and validate the analysis instrument set
source.pending_changes: The docker/ and evidence/ changes of this revision were uncommitted when the image was built; the binding identity of the toolchain is the image digest below, not the commit hash.

venue.note: Court recreated on the tools image. `status` prints cap_add, the effective CapEff of the container init process and whether capability 38 (CAP_PERFMON) is set, so the capability is observed rather than assumed.

venue_history.note: Revision-1 venue: already running and not recreated, with the instruments hand-installed into its writable layer. That layer (and /court/opam) was discarded by `down` during this revision; nothing from it is relied upon.

capability_change.change: docker/openssl-rs-court.sh now passes --cap-add=CAP_PERFMON at container creation, controlled by OPENSSL_RS_COURT_CAP_PERFMON (default 1; 0 reproduces the previous, perf-denied venue).
capability_change.why_creation_time: --cap-add cannot be applied by `docker update` to a running container, and CAP_PERFMON is not in docker's default capability set, so perf_event_open(2) returned EPERM no matter what was installed inside

observed_delta.delta: exactly bit 38 (CAP_PERFMON); no other bit changed

capability_change.grants: Only the kernel capability checks that perf_event_open(2) and perf's related privileged accesses consult, so that unprivileged-in-capability terms perf measurement of this container's own processes becomes permitted.
does_not_grant: CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_PTRACE or any other capability: CapDrop is unchanged and CapBnd/CapEff differ from the default set only in bit 38

seccomp relief: --security-opt seccomp=unconfined was NOT added and the profile was NOT replaced; /proc/self/status still reports Seccomp: 2 with 1 filter, and perf_event_open is permitted by docker's default profile already (a 1 filter count is what it was in revision 1)
a weaker no-new-privileges setting: --security-opt no-new-privileges is still passed, NoNewPrivs: 1
any change to kernel.perf_event_paranoid: it stays 2 and read-only in the container, so it cannot be lowered from inside
access to kernel-inclusive hardware counters where the paranoid gate or the absence of a PMU denies them
anything on the host: the capability is scoped to this container's own processes
capability_change.seccomp_profile: unchanged: docker's default profile, seccomp mode 2 with 1 filter, exactly as in revision 1
capability_change.measured_effect: perf_event_open(2) for software events went from EPERM to success; hardware 'cycles'/'instructions' are still unavailable, but for a different reason (no PMU exposed to this virtualised host), recorded under tools[perf].

negative_control.how: same image, same court script, same 16g-style caps, but OPENSSL_RS_COURT_CAP_PERFMON=0 on a throwaway 1g container (name openssl-rs-court-capprobe, removed afterwards)
negative_control.perf_output: perf stat -e task-clock /tmp/trivial -> 'No permission to enable task-clock event.' (revision-1 failure reproduced)
negative_control.conclusion: the capability is what changed the outcome: the launcher's default adds exactly the bit that turns EPERM into a measurement, and `status` distinguishes the two venues without being told which one it is looking at

tools.name: valgrind

persisted_image.pin_verified_at_build: dpkg-query version equality asserted by openssl-rs-court-tools-install.sh

tools.observed_output_signature: stdout 'trivial ok', no memcheck diagnostics, exit 0
limitations: Memcheck is a dynamic instrument; only executed paths are observed.
Court is shared/virtualised: no claim of quiet-machine timing.

tools.name: ctgrind (technique, not the abandoned patched-valgrind fork)
tools.install_command: no separate install; the pinned valgrind package ships memcheck.h/valgrind.h (the legacy ctgrind fork was NOT built)

persisted_image.path: inherits valgrind; headers asserted present at build (/usr/include/valgrind/{valgrind,memcheck}.h)

tools.observed_output_signature_revision_1:
==NNNN== Conditional jump or move depends on uninitialised value(s)
==NNNN==    at 0x109412: main (ctgrind_probe.c:26)
...
==NNNN== ERROR SUMMARY: 16 errors from 1 contexts (suppressed: 0 from 0), exit 99
tools.observed_output_signature_revision_2: identical: 'Conditional jump or move depends on uninitialised value(s) at 0x109412: main (ctgrind_probe.c:26)', 'ERROR SUMMARY: 16 errors from 1 contexts (suppressed: 0 from 0)', exit 99

sensitivity_control.positive: 16 errors from 1 contexts (one per loop iteration) for the buffer marked via VALGRIND_MAKE_MEM_UNDEFINED; exit 99
sensitivity_control.negative: identical program without the taint marker: 'ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors from 0 contexts', exit 0 (re-observed in the recreated court)
sensitivity_control.conclusion: the tool reports the deliberate secret-dependent branch and stays silent without the taint, so the detector is sensitive, not merely silent

limitations: Detects secret-dependent control flow and secret-dependent memory addresses only.
Does NOT detect variable-latency instructions (e.g. division/multiplication) on secret data.
Secret marking is a source-level client request; unmarked secrets are invisible to the tool.

tools.name: perf
tools.status_scope: HISTORICAL. This is the revision-1 verdict, in the ephemeral court with docker's default capability set. It is preserved verbatim as negative evidence and is superseded (not deleted) by resolved_by.
tools.status_in_persisted_image: FUNCTIONAL for software events (task-clock, cpu-clock, page-faults, context-switches); hardware PMU counters are UNAVAILABLE in this venue for a non-capability reason (see hardware_counters)

persisted_image.pin_verified_at_build: dpkg-query version equality asserted by openssl-rs-court-tools-install.sh

tools.validation_command_revision_1: perf stat -e task-clock ./trivial ; perf stat -e cycles ./trivial ; court/tmp/tools/perf_probe (direct perf_event_open(2))
tools.observed_output_signature_revision_1: perf: 'Error: No permission to enable task-clock event.' / 'No permission to enable cycles event.'; direct syscall: 'sw/task-clock exclude_kernel: FAIL errno=1 (Operation not permitted)' for task-clock, cpu-clock and cpu-cycles alike

blocker_revision_1.kind: capability restriction of the court container, not a missing install
blocker_revision_1.evidence: perf_event_open(2) returns EPERM even with exclude_kernel=1, which precedes the kernel's paranoid gate (that path returns EACCES); /proc/self/status reports Seccomp: 2 with 1 filter and NoNewPrivs: 1
blocker_revision_1.secondary: kernel.perf_event_paranoid=2 for kernel-inclusive events, and CapEff=0x00000000a80425fb includes neither CAP_PERFMON nor CAP_SYS_ADMIN; /proc/sys/kernel/perf_event_paranoid is read-only in the container, so it cannot be raised from inside
blocker_revision_1.what_would_unblock: docker run with a seccomp profile that permits perf_event_open (or seccomp=unconfined) plus CAP_PERFMON, and perf_event_paranoid<=1 for kernel events; this is a docker/ change, out of scope for this batch
blocker_revision_1.correction_in_revision_2: The seccomp half of that guess was wrong: docker's default profile does permit perf_event_open(2). The capability was the whole blocker. seccomp was therefore left untouched (no unconfined, no custom profile), and CAP_SYS_ADMIN was not needed.

tools.capability_note_revision_1: 'perf list' succeeds and enumerates 1353 events; that exercises the binary's event tables only and proves no measurement capability.
tools.observed_counters_revision_2: task-clock 0.33 msec (0.771 CPUs utilized), page-faults 54, minor-faults 54, context-switches 0; elapsed 0.000433209 s; perf exit 0. A second run reported task-clock 0.47 msec, 0.801 CPUs utilized, exit 0.
tools.direct_syscall_probe_revision_2: sw/task-clock exclude_kernel: OK fd=3; sw/cpu-clock kernel-incl: OK fd=3; hw/cpu-cycles exclude_kernel: FAIL errno=2 (No such file or directory) — the syscall is now permitted; the hardware event type does not exist in this venue

hardware_counters.evidence: perf stat -e cycles,instructions reports '<not supported>'; /sys/bus/event_source/devices lists breakpoint, kprobe, msr, power, software, tracepoint, uprobe but NOT 'cpu', i.e. no hardware PMU is exposed to this virtualised host; hw/cpu-cycles fails perf_event_open with ENOENT rather than EPERM
hardware_counters.consequence: instruction/cycle counts and IPC are not obtainable here; time-like software events are. This is an environment limit, not a permission that another flag can grant.
hardware_counters.not_attempted: CAP_SYS_ADMIN or a host-side PMU/paranoid change; neither would create a PMU device that the hypervisor does not expose, and CAP_SYS_ADMIN is explicitly out of scope.

tracepoints.evidence: perf stat -e sched:sched_process_exec -> 'Unable to find debugfs/tracefs' (debugfs is not mounted in the container)

limitations: Installed perf is 6.1.x while the kernel is 7.3.4; version skew remains an untested risk, though software-event measurement succeeds.
Software events only in this venue: no PMU, no tracepoints.

tools.name: dudect
tools.install_command: git clone https://github.com/oreparaz/dudect.git /opt/dudect && git -C /opt/dudect checkout --detach dc269651fb2567e46755cfb2a13d3875592968b5 && make -C /opt/dudect dut_simple dut_donnabad

persisted_image.pin_verified_at_build: checkout asserted before and after build (git rev-parse HEAD = pinned commit)

tools.observed_output_signature_revision_1: meas:    0.01 M, max t:  +67.38, max tau: 6.46e-01, (5/tau)^2: 5.99e+01. Probably not constant time.
tools.observed_output_signature_revision_2: meas:    0.01 M, max t:  +65.29, max tau: 6.26e-01, (5/tau)^2: 6.38e+01. Probably not constant time.

sensitivity_control.positive: dut_donnabad (upstream's deliberately leaky curve25519) terminates with max t=+65.29 (revision 1: +67.38), far above the |t|>5 threshold
sensitivity_control.negative: dudect_simple_O2 (memcmp example) kept reporting 'max t: +1.1x ... maybe constant time' until killed by timeout(1) at 133.8 M measurements; this is a NON-DETECTION, not evidence that memcmp is constant-time (both input classes in that example diverge at the first byte)
sensitivity_control.conclusion: the leaky control still separates cleanly from the t-test noise floor; max t varies run to run, as the statistic requires

limitations: Welch's t-test is statistical: absence of a detected difference is not a proof of constant-time behaviour.
Results are environment-bound (shared/virtualised CPU, frequency scaling, scheduler); no quiet-machine claim is made.
Needs a fixed number of measurements; long-running by design, so runs must be bounded with timeout(1).

tools.name: BINSEC
tools.install_command: opam init --bare --disable-sandboxing -n; opam switch create 4.14.2 ocaml-base-compiler.4.14.2 --jobs=4; opam switch import --switch 4.14.2 docker/openssl-rs-court-tools.opam-switch.export

extra_dependency.name: unisim_archisec.0.0.14
extra_dependency.why: without it, symbolic execution fails with '[sse:fatal] Can not resolve decoder for x86-64'

tools.historical_status: FUNCTIONAL (ephemeral court, revision 1; opam root was /court/opam)

persisted_image.path: OPAMROOT=/opt/opam, switch 4.14.2, binary on PATH at /opt/opam/4.14.2/bin/binsec
persisted_image.pin_verified_at_build: opam switch export --full --freeze (35 packages, URLs and archive checksums embedded) imported; installed set diffed against the export's installed list and required identical

tools.validation_command: gcc -nostdlib -static -no-pie -o tiny court/tmp/tools/tiny.s; printf 'starting from 0x401000\nreach 0x40100c\n' > /tmp/sse.cfg; binsec -sse -sse-script /tmp/sse.cfg -sse-depth 20 ./tiny
tools.observed_output_signature_revision_1: version: 'Binsec version 0.11.3'; SSE summary: 'total paths 1 / branching points 1 / discontinued paths 1 / visited instructions (static) 9 / max path depth 8'
tools.observed_output_signature_revision_2: version: 'Binsec version 0.11.3'; SSE summary: total paths 1, branching points 1, discontinued paths 1, visited instructions (static) 9, max path depth 8, exit 0 — identical to revision 1
limitations: The checkct constant-time plugin is NOT validated: 'binsec -checkct [-sse-script ...] ./tiny' exited 0 with no output at all, which is not a result; its configuration contract was not established in this batch.

'binsec -disasm ./trivial_static' (large static glibc ELF) aborted with an assertion failure in src/cli/command/disasm/disasm_core.ml:124 after printing a linear disassembly range; small freestanding ELFs are fine.
SSE needs an explicit reach goal; a bare '-sse' reports 'Nothing to reach' and explores nothing.
Symbolic execution covers the modelled ISA only; it does not observe real timing.

tools.name: TIMECOP
tools.version: poison.h method (upstream project dormant; no tagged release; SUPERCOP patches pinned to supercop-20181113/20190110/20190816)
tools.install_command: no install: the TIMECOP method is stock valgrind + poison.h (public-domain header from the project page); no patched valgrind was built

persisted_image.path: inherits valgrind; the header and example are the repository's court/tmp/tools/timecop_repro/{poison.h,example.c}

tools.method_validated: poison.h (VALGRIND_MAKE_MEM_UNDEFINED wrappers) over stock valgrind 3.19.0 with --track-origins=yes
tools.not_validated: the SUPERCOP-integrated TIMECOP harness (patch -p1 over a pinned SUPERCOP tree) was NOT attempted; see timecop_supercop_harness
tools.observed_output_signature_revision_1: two contexts: 'Conditional jump or move depends on uninitialised value(s) at ... modular_pow (example.c:14)' and '... (example.c:15)', each with 'Uninitialised value was created by a client request at ... main (example.c:29)'; 'ERROR SUMMARY: 61 errors from 2 contexts (suppressed: 0 from 0)'
tools.observed_output_signature_revision_2: identical: 2 'Conditional jump or move depends on uninitialised value(s)' contexts, both origins 'Uninitialised value was created by a client request', 'ERROR SUMMARY: 61 errors from 2 contexts (suppressed: 0 from 0)', valgrind error exit 93
tools.agreement_with_upstream: the upstream page documents the same result for this example (both secret-dependent branches reported, origin traced to the poison() call, 61 errors from 2 contexts)
limitations: Same property and same blind spots as the ctgrind technique: control flow and memory addresses only, no variable-time instructions.
The SUPERCOP harness is unmaintained and version-pinned; it would require a large pinned SUPERCOP tree and patch that may no longer apply.
Requires the secret to be marked with poison(); unmarked secrets are invisible.

timecop_supercop_harness.reason: Unmaintained project: upstream ships patches only for supercop-20181113, supercop-20190110 and supercop-20190816, requires the full SUPERCOP tree (2,700+ implementations), and its maintenance status is dormant. The secret-taint property it exists to check is reproduced on current Valgrind by the ctgrind/TIMECOP poison.h technique recorded above, so the short path (method reproduction) was taken and the long path (pinned SUPERCOP patch) was not.

rebuild.build_memory_cap: 8g, passed to BuildKit as --resource memory=8g by OPENSSL_RS_COURT_BUILD_MEM (the build runs outside the court, so it cannot be inside the court's cgroup)
rebuild.install_script: docker/openssl-rs-court-tools-install.sh (copied into the image at /opt/timing-tools/install.sh, so the image carries its own recipe)
rebuild.install_script_identity: the repository file and the copy inside the built image (/opt/timing-tools/install.sh) hash identically, so the shipped script is the one this image was built from; an earlier attempt failed on opam 2.1.2's lack of --no-header and on `opam switch create NAME` needing an explicit compiler, and was rebuilt after those corrections
determinism: apt packages pinned to exact bookworm versions and re-verified with dpkg-query after install; an unavailable pin fails the build
dudect pinned to a commit and asserted before and after build

the opam package set comes from `opam switch export --full --freeze`, which embeds every package definition with its archive URL and checksum; the installed set is diffed against the export's installed list and must be identical (35 packages)

the compiler package (ocaml-base-compiler.4.14.2) is requested explicitly and still comes from the opam repository index at build time; if that index stops offering 4.14.2 the build fails instead of silently substituting

build_result.warnings: none from the build itself; the second apt opam run printed opam's 'Running as root is not recommended' warning inside the build log, which is informational
build_result.earlier_failed_attempt: exit 2 on the first attempt at the run-time verification step (opam 2.1.2 has no --no-header); fixed in the install script, then rebuilt from a clean RUN layer

install_replay_ephemeral.note: HISTORICAL (revision 1): the exact ordered commands that recreated the toolchain by hand from a fresh openssl-rs-court:1 container. Superseded by the image at rebuild, kept because it is the record of what the ephemeral venue actually ran.
commands: DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends valgrind linux-perf opam bubblewrap patch m4 pkg-config unzip rsync libgmp-dev
git clone https://github.com/oreparaz/dudect.git && cd dudect && git checkout dc269651fb2567e46755cfb2a13d3875592968b5 && make dut_simple dut_donnabad

persistence.statement: Every instrument above is now a layer of openssl-rs-court-tools:1 (digest in venue), built from docker/openssl-rs-court-tools.Dockerfile. `docker/openssl-rs-court.sh down` still removes the container and its /court scratch space, but a court recreated with OPENSSL_RS_COURT_IMAGE=openssl-rs-court-tools:1 starts with valgrind/ctgrind headers, perf, dudect (/opt/dudect), BINSEC (OPAMROOT=/opt/opam, switch 4.14.2) and the TIMECOP poison.h headers already installed.
persistence.replaces: BINSEC's opam root moved from /court/opam (scratch, destroyed by `down`) to /opt/opam (image layer).
persistence.not_persisted: Nothing from the discarded container was carried over: the image was rebuilt from openssl-rs-court:1 plus the pinned install, not committed from the old container. The small test programs used for validation (trivial.c, ctgrind_probe.c, tiny.s, timecop_repro/) live in the repository bind mount under court/tmp/tools/ and are not part of the image.
persistence.scope: Separate tag, never selected implicitly. Conversion gates, forensic regeneration and the OOM-bounded Rust test loop keep running the minimal openssl-rs-court:1 unless the caller opts in.
persistence.known_consequence: `docker/openssl-rs-court.sh exec` records PHASE24_IMAGE/PHASE25_IMAGE from OPENSSL_RS_COURT_IMAGE, and forensics/downstream/container.json and forensics/memory-safety/container.json name openssl-rs-court:1. A court running the tools image is therefore not an admitted venue for the Phase-24/25 guards; timing-instrument runs must not invoke them.

revalidation.when: 2026-11-20, after the court was recreated on openssl-rs-court-tools:1 with --cap-add=CAP_PERFMON
results: perf stat -e task-clock,page-faults,minor-faults,context-switches ./trivial -> exit 0, counters reported (see tools[perf].observed_counters_revision_2)
ctgrind positive control -> 16 errors from 1 context, exit 99; untagged twin -> 0 errors from 0 contexts, exit 0
dudect dut_donnabad -> max t +65.29, 'Probably not constant time'
BINSEC -sse on the freestanding ELF -> 1 path, 1 branching point, 9 static instructions, exit 0
TIMECOP example.c -> 2 contexts, 61 errors from 2 contexts, origins from the client request

not_run: BINSEC checkct constant-time plugin (invocation produced no output; configuration contract not established).
Hardware PMU events (cycles/instructions) in this venue: no PMU device is exposed to the virtualised host; not attempted with CAP_SYS_ADMIN, which cannot create one.
perf tracepoints (debugfs/tracefs is not mounted in the container).
Any timing measurement of openssl-rs code: no dudect, valgrind or BINSEC run was performed against the crate or its test suite.
Release-profile builds, full test suite, clippy, fmt (no source change was made, so the §6 local gate was not invoked).
Persistence in the court image was the subject of revision 1's not_run list; it is now done and recorded above.
non_claims: This inventory is not evidence about the constant-timeness of any openssl-rs implementation; it records tool availability and detector sensitivity only.
The ctgrind/TIMECOP technique cannot see variable-latency instructions, and a clean run is not a constant-time proof.
dudect's t-test is statistical; a single run on a shared/virtualised CPU is not a timing verdict.
The presence of the perf binary and its 1353-entry 'perf list' output is not measurement capability; the capability is demonstrated only by the reported counters.

CAP_PERFMON is not a general privilege grant: it does not add CAP_SYS_ADMIN, does not weaken seccomp, does not weaken no-new-privileges, does not change perf_event_paranoid, and does not affect the host.
No claim is made that these tools behave identically to the pinned OpenSSL authority or to a quiet machine.
Nothing here is a §7 SAFETY_DISCHARGED or SAFE_COMPATIBLE promotion.
